[DECISION] INCOMPLETE

[FEEDBACK] Critical missing data required to support or refute papillary thyroid carcinoma: (1) Thyroid ultrasound (to identify nodule(s), assess size, echogenicity, margins, microcalcifications, vascularity); (2) Serum TSH and free T4 (to determine if thyroid dysfunction coexists); (3) Fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy of any suspicious nodule(s) identified on imaging; (4) Consider contrast-enhanced neck CT or esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) given persistent dysphagia without obvious thyroid mass — to exclude esophageal stricture, malignancy, or extrinsic compression. Without at least ultrasound + FNA, the diagnosis remains speculative.
